source: Original (authored 2026-11-17, no calculator, scaffolded). Graph of f(x) = 2 sin x + 1 on [0, 2pi] with y = sin x dashed; A max (pi/2, 3), B min (3pi/2, -1). Version c.

parts.label: a
parts.description: Write down the coordinates of the y-intercept.

parts.label: b
parts.description: Write down the coordinates of A (max) and B (min).
parts.tolerance: Accept 90 and 270 degrees for the x-coordinates.
parts.notes: A1 for each point; both coordinates needed for each mark.

parts.label: c
parts.description: Read the two x-intercepts from the grid.

parts.label: d
parts.description: Find d = (max + min)/2 and a = (max - min)/2.
parts.notes: A1 for each value; bare values earn the marks.
parts.follow_through: FT from the candidate's max and min in (b).

parts.label: f
parts.description: Complete: stretched vertically by scale factor __, then translated __ units up.

source: Original (authored 2026-11-17, no calculator, scaffolded). Unit circle: 60 deg to radians; cos and sin of pi/3; P at pi/4; Q at 135 deg (reflection of P in the y-axis); sin theta = 3/5 acute. Version c.

parts.label: b
parts.description: Write down exact cos(pi/3) and sin(pi/3).
parts.notes: A1 for each value. Values swapped: A0A0.

parts.label: c
parts.description: Exact coordinates of P at pi/4.

parts.label: d
parts.description: Exact coordinates of Q at 135 degrees.
parts.notes: A1 for each coordinate with its sign.
parts.follow_through: FT from (c) with the sign of the x-coordinate changed.

parts.label: e
parts.description: sin theta = 3/5, theta acute: find cos theta using sin^2 + cos^2 = 1.
parts.notes: M1 for cos^2 theta = 1 - 9/25 (or the hinted equation). A1 for 4/5. A bare 4/5 earns M0A1; +/- 4/5 as the final answer earns M1A0.

source: Original (authored 2026-11-17, calculator, degrees, scaffolded). Triangle ABC: AB = 5, AC = 8, angle BAC = 60 deg. Version c.

parts.label: a
parts.description: Find BC with the cosine rule.
parts.notes: M1 for the cosine rule. A1 for 5^2 + 8^2 - 2(5)(8) cos 60. A1 for 7. Wrong method: radian mode gives 12.9: M1A1A0.

parts.label: b
parts.description: Find the area with (1/2)(AB)(AC) sin A.
parts.tolerance: Accept 10sqrt3. Accept 3 s.f. or the calculator display with an ellipsis; a value cut short with no ellipsis earns A0 (markscheme-spec 21).

parts.label: c
parts.description: Find angle ACB with the sine rule.
parts.tolerance: Accept any value consistent with the candidate's own correctly-rounded intermediate values; note premature rounding as feedback rather than withholding the accuracy mark. Accept 3 s.f. or the calculator display with an ellipsis; a value cut short with no ellipsis earns A0 (markscheme-spec 21).
parts.notes: M1 for the sine rule. A1 for pairing AB = 5 with angle C and BC with 60 deg. A1 for 38.2. Wrong method: pairing 8 with angle C gives 81.8 (angle ABC): M1A0A0.
parts.follow_through: FT from the candidate's BC in (a).

source: Original (authored 2026-11-17, calculator, radians, scaffolded). N(t) = 2.9 sin(pi/6 (t - 2.7)) + 12.2 (New York), P(t) = 2.65 sin(pi/6 (t - 2.7)) + 12.15 (Palermo), t months after 1 January. Version c.

parts.label: a
parts.description: Write down the max and min daylight in New York.
parts.notes: A1 for each value (d + a and d - a).

parts.label: b
parts.description: Find the period of N in months.
parts.notes: M1 for 2pi/(pi/6). A1 for 12. A bare 12 earns M0A1.

parts.label: c
parts.tolerance: Accept 3 s.f. or the calculator display with an ellipsis; a value cut short with no ellipsis earns A0 (markscheme-spec 21).
parts.notes: M1 for substituting t = 10.5. A1 for 9.85. Wrong method: degree mode gives 12.4: M1A0.

parts.label: d
parts.description: Write down the max and min daylight in Palermo.

parts.label: e
parts.description: How many more minutes of daylight Palermo has on the shortest day.
parts.notes: M1 for 9.5 - 9.3 (difference of the minima). A1 for 12 minutes. Wrong method: 0.2 with no conversion: M1A0.
